## Summary

```text
three authored slots → receive default → initialize preview/listeners
missing default       → keep loading
child visit/return    → retain cards, canvases, fits and art age
```

Preserves UpgradeMenu loading independently of motion: cached/live class inputs, null-result counters, ordered recenter/removal behavior, root frames1–4 and the imported five-dot loader. Creator return reuses initialized offers without preference rerolls. Selection removes card handlers while bottom input remains live.

Layer1 of the next five-PR batch. Assemble all layers in the last PR and validate its combined head before one master merge. Batch branches use `stack/**` to suppress automatic previews.

## Evidence

- **Before:** compressed available offers appeared ready immediately; child visits recreated previews and rerolled offers.
  **After:** stable slots and pending loading survive, with retained preview paint source/canvas/fit/age.
- Formatting, TypeScript, 903 unit tests / 8,342 assertions and production builds passed.
- Literal `bun run test:e2e`: all8 mock/supplied-SWF cases passed, zero skips/flaky cases, across upgrade-loading, upgrade-presentation, upgrade-defaults and edit-flow. Paint inspected in both modes; checks include Chromium accessibility, pending-menu keyboard activation, renderer identity, reversal and teardown.
- Import regenerates byte-identically; old ready-menu geometry/widgets remain unchanged. No media/dependency/build output committed.
- Unsaved automatic return has source/service coverage without a direct browser case. Lazy preview readiness is an explicit browser adapter; constructor/RNG/frame scheduling, Adobe and full-game parity remain unproved.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** upgrade

Changes loading/input and retained child-view lifetime. Require current-head Actions and actionable-review gates; hold master integration for the five-layer batch. Vercel quota failures are waived; no deployment retries/account changes.

## Summary

Returning to an uncleared field previously discarded a Healer's beam reference because the fresh wrapper did not list it. Incoming boss spawners also created fighters in the incoming wrapper and ran them a frame early. The source keeps the old beam parent and routes boss births through the outgoing currentBFTarget.

```text
cached Healer → retained old-layer beam → outgoing-coordinate update
incoming boss → outgoing wrapper → newborn Run on its next actor pass
```

Keep StopFiring's source current-wrapper removal request, including its no-op for an older-layer beam. Projectile-parent bookkeeping stays in simulation.

This PR now contains authored loading from #130 plus this cross-field ownership layer. Both heads are verified ancestors of the combined [PR #134](https://github.com/ianwijma/open-bubble-tank/pull/134). It targets master so that final merge accounts for the included commits; use #134's combined gate and do not merge this layer independently. Preview suppression is inherited; provider-confirmed skipping remains unverified.

## Evidence

- **Before:** cached-Healer identity and incoming-boss ownership regressions failed.
  **After:** all 907 unit tests / 8,390 assertions pass, including four ownership regressions; formatting and TypeScript pass.
- Production build and literal `bun run test:e2e` passed all six affected mock/supplied-SWF Healer lifecycle, targeting and actor behavior cases, with zero skips or page errors. Paint captures were inspected. Private fixture copies changed only the transport port.
- Browser fixtures cover adjacent paint/contact/lifecycle behavior. The two cross-field paths are source/unit checked; synchronized original/Adobe/full-game parity remains unproved. Source contracts and scoped limits are in `docs/cross-field-weapons-reference.md`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert the simulation changes to roll back; no saved-data migration.

**Blast Radius:** combat

Changes retained projectile-parent bookkeeping and wrapper ownership for boss births. No original media or build artifacts included.

## Summary

Boss spawners previously chose a fighter on their first shot. The original chooses each mount's fighter during Setup, so later roster growth cannot change it and later part constructors receive the correct random draws. Cache the selection after target acquisition and use the source rounded inclusive index.

```text
register spawner → acquire target → cache fighter → construct next detail
fire → spawn cached fighter in outgoing wrapper
```

This PR now contains layers 1–3, with cached fighter Setup as its focused change. All included heads are verified ancestors of the combined [PR #134](https://github.com/ianwijma/open-bubble-tank/pull/134). It targets master so that final merge accounts for these commits; use #134's combined gate and do not merge this layer independently. The handoff records that delivery policy.

## Evidence

- **Before:** both new regressions failed: missing Setup choice and an unexpected fighter-selection draw during firing.
  **After:** 909 unit tests / 8,395 assertions pass, including acquisition/selection/Phasing ordering, rounded-index boundary, independent mounts, roster growth and repeated shots. Formatting and TypeScript pass.
- Production build and literal `bun run test:e2e` passed all six mock/supplied-SWF actor, mounted-targeting and accelerated boss/win cases: zero failures, skips, flaky cases or page errors. Every assertion was retained; private copies changed only the fixture transport port. Owned servers stopped.
- Pilots reached all six upgrades, boss defeat, badge and Continue: 82,489 mock / 77,617 supplied-art frames. Supplied-art history and win paint were inspected. The pilots use seeded accelerated simulation and an upgrade-selection adapter; they do not establish ordinary-input progression or original-runtime parity.
- `docs/cross-field-weapons-reference.md` records the ActionScript/pcode call order and remaining complete-constructor/RNG, missing-roster and original/Adobe limits. The existing standalone-tool fallback remains explicit.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No saved-data migration; revert to undo the timing correction.

**Blast Radius:** combat

Changing when spawners consume randomness intentionally changes later generated choices. No source media or build output is included. The stack branch inherits preview suppression; provider-confirmed skipping remains unverified.

Created with GPT-6.1 Sol in T3 Code's Codex harness.

caller finishes field tail → 19 save-before-blurs → Run40 raises frame2
